 One Leicester City change for Stevenage as Conor Chaplin and John Lundstram decision made
 Leicester City come into tomorrow's game against Stevenage on the back of a big win over Wigan Athletic
 View 4 Images Conor Chaplin (Image: 2026 CameraSport) 
 Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Josh Holland Leicester City correspondent 12:00, 30 Oct 2026 Leicester City's busy run of League One fixtures comes to an end tomorrow afternoon when they face Stevenage at the King Power Stadium.
 The Foxes returned to winning ways on Tuesday night, with Emil Riis' brace helping them to a 3-0 victory over Wigan Athletic. The result gives Russell Martin three wins from his side's last four games, leaving Leicester five points off the automatic promotion places.
 Saturday's meeting with Stevenage is Leicester's final league fixture for several weeks, with their FA Cup campaign beginning in seven days before next month's international break. City faced Alex Revell's side in the Jersey Mike's Trophy earlier this month, losing 2-1 as Wanya Marçal scored against his former club.
 Martin made two changes for the Wigan game after naming the same starting XI for three consecutive matches. John Lundstram is available again after serving his suspension, leaving Martin with another selection decision. Here's how LeicestershireLive expects Leicester to line up against Stevenage.
 ‌

 Martin's favourite trio
 Alex McCarthy kept another clean sheet against Wigan and is beginning to look increasingly assured in goal. His injury-time save to deny Morgan Fox was exceptional, while his distribution has also improved.
 The back three looked more assured against Wigan than they had at Luton, although vulnerabilities remained. Scott Hogan was given too much room to bear down on goal, while Dara Costelloe was left unmarked when the ball came into the box.
 Warren O'Hora and Caleb Okoli both improved against Wigan, but Harry Souttar remains the most secure of the three in his place. Martin has also indicated that Ilari Kangasniemi is pushing for an opportunity , saying: "I think I really like the back three and what they've done over the last few games. There's a lot of experience there. But Ilari's really chomping at the bit underneath that and you saw that tonight."
 ‌ 
 View 4 Images Ilari Kangasniemi played as an attacking wing-back off the bench against Wigan (Image: MI News/NurPhoto) 
 Will Alves and Luke Thomas should retain their places at wing-back, having struck a useful balance in the system. Alves provides the attacking threat, while Thomas offers a more measured option on the opposite flank.
 Smallbone tweak and dilemmas
 Lundstram is likely to return to the starting XI after suspension, meaning Martin will have to adjust his midfield four. The manager has also hinted that Will Smallbone will play further forward than he did against Wigan , which could influence how the midfield is configured.
 View 4 Images Will Smallbone made his first start for Leicester City against Wigan (Image: 2026 Plumb Images) 
 ‌ 
 Louis Page impressed against Wigan on Tuesday and has benefited from Lundstram's arrival alongside him in midfield. Smallbone is expected to play further forward alongside Kamari Doyle, leaving Conor Chaplin, Liam Cullen and Sammy Braybrooke out of the starting XI.
 Difficult decision in attack
 The attacking-midfield positions present Martin with his biggest selection dilemma. Braybrooke impressed after coming off the bench against Wigan, while Chaplin offers a significant goal threat. Doyle, however, has been consistent throughout Leicester's recent run.
 Riis looks certain to lead the line. Only five players have scored more than the striker in League One this season, despite him missing the opening four games, and Martin believes there is more to come.
 View 4 Images Emil Riis celebrates putting Leicester City 2-0 up (Image: 2026 Getty Images) 
 ‌ 
 "He's going to get better, he's going to get fitter because he hasn't really had a pre-season," Martin said. "He's a man, he takes hits and he takes the ball for us. He runs hard, he presses like a beast and tonight, he was in the right position to score two goals.
 "On Saturday, he was trying to do a bit too much, was my feeling and then we just sat down and looked at it together. Now he has someone like Steve Morison, who played in that position. They can chat a lot, it's not a position I know very well.
 "To have someone like Steve to bounce a few things off is really important. I really enjoyed him tonight."
 Predicted starting line-up to face Stevenage: McCarthy; O'Hora, Souttar, Okoli; Alves, Lundstram, Page, Thomas; Smallbone, Doyle, Riis.
